subject: Post-demo: log snapshot delivery options & PII scope confirmation
messages:
From: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>
To: Alex Huang <alex.huang@clearskyhealth.com>, Priya Shah <priya.shah@clearskyhealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-08-20T15:03:00-07:00
Subject: Post-demo: log snapshot delivery options & PII scope confirmation

Hi Alex / Priya —

Thanks again for taking the demo earlier. Quick recap and the actions we discussed so we can get your security/compliance team the right artifacts: 

- You asked for a sample "who viewed what and when" export for the last 30 days (transactional level) and a small playback sample showing exact API requests that touched identifiable fields.
- You also want confirmation on how Redwood surfaces PII in logs, options for redaction/pseudonymization, and the minimum retention window we can support.

Proposed next steps from our side:
1) I can send a redwood_who_when_schema.csv (column-level mapping) and a 48-row sample_playback.jsonl (anonymized) by EOD tomorrow.
2) If you need raw identifiers surfaced (email/user-id), we'll need a signed Request for Logs form from your security team.
3) We can outline two delivery formats: CSV with timestamped rows (easy to ingest) or JSONL with request/response playback (better for forensic replay).

Do you have a preference for CSV vs JSONL? Also, can you confirm the exact set of object types you want included (user profile, document id, prompt text, embed id, etc.) — I included a draft scope in the attached PDF.

If it's helpful, I can loop in Ben from our Security Sales team to answer the KMS / redaction questions.

Rafael Mendes
Senior Account Executive\Redwood Inference
rafael.mendes@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0192

Attachments: redwood_who_when_schema.csv, sample_playback.jsonl, redwood_pii_scope.pdf

From: Alex Huang <alex.huang@clearskyhealth.com>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>
Cc: Priya Shah <priya.shah@clearskyhealth.com>
Date: 2027-08-20T17:11:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo: log snapshot delivery options & PII scope confirmation

Rafael —

Thanks for the clear recap. A couple clarifications from our side before we take this to security: 

1) Scope: we want user account identifiers (email hash acceptable), document id, operation type (read/write), timestamp, and the API route. We do NOT need prompt text in the sample — but we need to know whether prompt text can appear in any logged field and how it would be redacted.

2) Format: JSONL preferred for the playback sample for our engineering team. For the audit CSV, CSV is fine.

3) Retention: we need options for 90 days default, with the ability to request 12 months for legal holds. Is that supported via an export request or a config change?

4) Evidence: security asked for a small example of the export in both formats plus a short explanation of how Redwood ensures that only authorized roles can request exports (audit trail + approvals).

If you can include who in Redwood has access to the export tooling and whether KMS-wrapped logs are an option, that would be great. Once we have the sample, we'll route to our compliance reviewer and send the signed request if needed.

— Alex
Head of Infrastructure, ClearSky Health
alex.huang@clearskyhealth.com

From: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>
To: Alex Huang <alex.huang@clearskyhealth.com>, Priya Shah <priya.shah@clearskyhealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-08-20T20:08:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo: log snapshot delivery options & PII scope confirmation

Alex —

Perfect, thanks for the specifics. Quick answers inline and plan: 

- Prompt text: Redwood will not include prompt text in the CSV audit export by default. For playback.jsonl we can include prompt text only after an explicit, signed export request and with a documented approval workflow. If you prefer prompt text redacted, we can pseudonymize (SHA256 with salt) or remove entirely.

- Formats: I'll attach the sample_playback.jsonl (anonymized) and a CSV sample based on the redwood_who_when_schema.csv.

- Retention: We support configurable retention per tenant. Default hosted retention is 90 days; we can enable 12 months for accounts under a managed retention policy — that requires a written order and is surfaced as a tenant-level setting (we'll provide the change request template).

- Authorization & audit trail: Exports are gated by role-based permissions. Every export request generates an immutable audit record (who requested, approver id, timestamp, exported object types). We can provide a screenshot of the export approval UI or a CSV extract with the approval events. KMS: For Private deployments we support bringing-your-own-KMS for encrypting stored logs; for Hosted we manage keys but can enable envelope encryption and HSM-wrapped keys on enterprise plans.

Action items I will take now: 
- Send the two sample files (CSV + JSONL) and the redwood_pii_scope.pdf that outlines field-level PII exposure and recommended redaction approach.
- Send a one-page export request template your security team can sign.

If that's good, expect the bundle tomorrow morning. Ben, can you add any technical/controls notes on the export audit trail and approver flow?

Thanks,
Rafael

Rafael / Ben —

Quick internal note: Per Alex's asks, Security wants the following bullet points covered in the handoff doc we send to ClearSky:

- Exact schema fields we will include in CSV vs JSONL (include example rows).
- The signed export request workflow + the minimum approval chain (requestor -> engineering security approver).
- How prompt text is handled for both Hosted and Private deployments (redaction/pseudonymization options).
- Retention options and the process to enable 12-month retention or legal hold.
- KMS/HSM options for log encryption and whether keys are customer-managed for Private.

Ben, can you draft 2–3 lines on the export approval audit trail (what fields the audit contains) and confirm whether we can produce an approvals CSV sample? Aim to have this draft ready before Rafael sends the bundle to ClearSky so we don't do another revision.

Marissa Cole
